_comment: The agent table (plan 019 §3.2; shrunk to two rows by plan 025 C2, shed#390):
kind -> binary -> title, for the agents the `shed roost-provider` menu can
start in a roost tab. Codex, cursor, gx and grok left this table in plan
025 — craze is now the lane for every provider but Claude and opencode, and
its own create sheet (not this roost menu) is the launch surface for it.
NOT a roost vector — see this directory's README, section 'shed's own
multi-language goldens'. This file is shed's, and it may be edited; the
no-semantic-edits rule applies to the vendored vectors around it.
Asserted from three places, which is the whole point:
- Go: internal/roostprovider/goldens_test.go, against `agentTable`.
- Rust: crates/shed-core/tests/roost_provider_vectors.rs, against
`shed_core::roost::model::launch_argv` (kind -> binary) and against
`roost_capabilities().kinds` (the kind SET).
- Dart: shed-mobile's integration_test/roost_goldens_test.dart, against
the ROOST-BACKED launch kinds (not the machine create form's full set,
which also offers craze — plan 025 CM2 re-scopes that assertion). It
reads this file out of a shed checkout named by $SHED_CHECKOUT.
Order is the PROVIDER's display order — `claude opencode`, pinned by §3.2
(the probe's `command -v` list and the 'no agents found' subtitle). It
differs from `roost_capabilities().kinds`'s own order only in principle now
that both are two rows; the Rust test still compares them as sets, never as
sequences, since one is a capabilities advertisement and the other a menu.
The three spellings are not interchangeable: `claude-rc` is the RC wire kind,
`claude` is the binary on the far side, and the titles are what a human
reads in roost's palette.
